adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code adds a fetch call to refresh tokens (lines 72-89) directly in what appears to be the getClient/init method. Unlike other calendar services in this diff (like GoogleCalendarService, Office365CalendarService) which wrap their refresh logic in a `refreshAccessToken` function that checks token expiry before refreshing, the Salesforce implementation unconditionally calls the token refresh endpoint. The code at line 72-89 shows `const response = await fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` without any expiry check, and this is in the main credential initialization flow. This means every time the service is instantiated (likely per API request), it will make an external refresh call, which is inefficient and could cause rate limiting issues with Salesforce's OAuth endpoint.
